title: Bran born to the north-west shore
summary: Bran is born to a fishing hearth of the north-west shore, kin who keep Aithris a' Chruthachaidh as every hill hearth does but hear its westward part first, the part that names Tìr nan Òg, Magh Meall and Taigh Dhuinn across the open sea.

title: The best boatman of that coast
summary: Grown to a man, Bran is known the length of the north-west shore as the surest hand with a swell and a stitching-needle alike, mending hulls that no other boatman's seams will hold and reading weather other men cannot.

title: Bran begins the great hull
summary: Bran starts gathering bull-hides cured harder and longer than any boat on his coast has needed, and sets ribs of hazel and ash closer than a hand's width, telling his kin at first only that he means a bigger boat for a bigger catch.

title: Bran tells his mother the boat's purpose
summary: Two winters into the building, Bran tells his mother plainly that he means to sail west and prove Aithris a' Chruthachaidh's word of a land beyond the sea's edge true or false. She does not forbid him, though she warns him no telling yet has anyone to bring it home.

title: The great hull finished
summary: By the second spring Bran's boat stands finished on its trestles, broader and higher at the bow than any craft that coast has built, decked with sealed skins to throw off green water, built plainly for open sea rather than the shallows.

title: Blàthnaid's promise asked and given
summary: The night before the boat puts out, Blàthnaid asks her brother Bran to tell her the truth of whatever he finds, if ever he has the chance. He promises it, a promise she keeps for the rest of her life though he never returns to be asked again.

title: Bran sails west
summary: In high summer Bran puts out from the north-west shore with four kinsmen, holding his bow south of the grey bank that never lifts off the northern sea and west into open water no boat of that coast has crossed before. The household sends them off in silence.

title: The crewman found on the southern shingle
summary: A season and more after the boat put out, a woman gathering shellfish finds the youngest of the crew, Bran's sister's son, alive but near dead on a stretch of shingle two days south of his home shore, sun-blackened and too parched to speak.

title: The boy's telling of the green land
summary: Over days of broken whispers the crewman tells of many days on open water, then a green land rising from the sea where fruit hung ready and a spring broke sweet from the rock, and a welcome from a people unmarked by age.

title: Bran stays in the west
summary: The crewman tells that Bran, offered his freedom to turn home, chose to stay on the green shore, saying he would not turn from the question he had followed his whole life to answer now that his feet stood on it.

title: The crewman dies
summary: Eleven days after he is carried in from the shingle, Bran's sister's son dies with the door left open on the sea, saying to the last that the land had not been unkind and his uncle had not looked afraid.

title: The telling spreads along the coast
summary: Within a year of the boy's death the telling of the green land in the west has gone the length of the north-west shore and inland besides, growing surer in each mouth than the dying boy ever claimed it.

title: A boy nearly follows the telling west
summary: A fifteen-year-old of the shore is found in the dark sitting in a coracle he has no business taking out, looking west, and is brought home and wept over, the telling's first plain harm.

title: The elders let the telling fall
summary: The elders of three shore households agree at a closed fire to starve the telling of the green land rather than forbid it outright, answering no stranger's question of it and teaching it to no child who has not already heard it.

title: Blàthnaid tells her daughter, once
summary: An old woman by then, Blàthnaid keeps her promise the only way left to her, telling her grown daughter the whole of the boy's account at a covered hearth, and naming her brother at the end of it: Bran.

title: Blàthnaid dies
summary: Blàthnaid dies an old woman, having told the steersman's telling to no one but her own daughter, who carries it on in the same low voice at the same covered fire.
